source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

china_plus_one.evidence: BEL is a key Atmanirbhar Bharat/Make in India beneficiary; 90%+ of products are indigenously developed and manufactured. Management explicitly frames self-reliance in defence electronics as a supply-chain-diversification opportunity for the Indian armed forces. Order book includes indigenous radar systems, electronic warfare, communication equipment, and missile systems under the defence indigenisation push.

govt_capex.evidence: BEL is a defence PSU; approximately 90% of revenue is from the defence sector (MoD orders). Key product categories include radar systems, electronic warfare, military communication, night-vision devices, and integrated missile systems. FY2024-25 revenue ~Rs 21,693 crore; defence revenue ~Rs 19,500 crore. Non-defence revenue (civilian radar, solar, medical electronics) accounts for remaining ~10%.

rate_sensitive.evidence: BEL maintains a net cash-positive balance sheet; net cash/investments of approximately Rs 11,000 crore as of FY25. No significant interest-bearing borrowings disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export revenue ~Rs 870 crore (~4% of FY25 total revenue) including exports to friendly foreign countries for defence equipment. USD-INR hedging policy not separately disclosed in accessible sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: BEL is a government PSU and is not a PLI scheme beneficiary in the manufacturing incentive sense. BEL participates in DPP offset obligations and indigenisation programs but not the commercial PLI scheme.

govt_capex.evidence: Siemens India's Energy and Smart Infrastructure segments serve Indian Railways (IGBT-based propulsion, metro rail traction), power T&D utilities, and government-linked infrastructure projects. Government capex-linked revenue % not explicitly disclosed. Siemens India uses October–September fiscal year; FY2023-24 = year ended September 2024.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Siemens India is debt-free with a net cash-positive balance sheet. Not materially rate-sensitive on liability side.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export revenue ~18% of total revenue in FY2023-24. Siemens India exports industrial equipment, drive systems, and energy solutions to global markets through parent Siemens AG network. Specific USD % of exports and hedging policy not disclosed in accessible sources.

china_plus_one.evidence: Lupin has reduced dependence on China for active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) to below 30% of API sourcing and is actively backward integrating into KSM/API manufacturing. Management cited India's API PLI scheme as enabling supply chain diversification. Global pharma companies' shift away from China API sourcing is highlighted as a medium-term demand driver for Lupin's API and CDMO businesses.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Natural hedges (USD import costs partially offset USD export receipts) supplemented by forex derivatives including forward exchange contracts in USD. Cash flow hedge accounting applied.
inr_exposure.evidence: US business revenue ~38% of total revenue in FY2024-25 (Lupin's largest single geography). Total exports ~66% of revenue. Natural hedge through USD-denominated API imports netting against export receipts.

pli_scheme.evidence: Lupin is a confirmed beneficiary of India's PLI scheme for Bulk Drugs (KSM/APIs). The company received PLI scheme approval for several API products and is investing in API/KSM manufacturing capacity at Aurangabad and other sites to qualify for incremental production incentives.

china_plus_one.evidence: ABB India MD Sanjeev Sharma articulated a 'local for local' manufacturing strategy positioning India as an export hub for ABB Group globally in CY2024. The company is positioning Indian manufacturing (robotics, drives, switchgear) for export to markets where global customers are diversifying supply chains away from China. ABB India exports to Middle East, Southeast Asia, and Africa. ABB India uses January–December fiscal year; CY2024 = year ended December 2024.

govt_capex.evidence: ABB India serves railways (traction systems, DC traction motors), power utilities, data centers, renewable energy (solar, wind), and industrial infrastructure. Government capex-linked revenue % not explicitly disclosed; key end-markets include Dedicated Freight Corridor, Indian Railways electrification, and state utility T&D modernisation.

rate_sensitive.evidence: ABB India has a net cash position of approximately Rs 10,965 crore as of end-CY2024. No significant debt; not materially rate-sensitive on liability side.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export revenue ~10% of total CY2024 revenue (~Rs 1,282 crore out of ~Rs 12,825 crore). ABB India exports to 90+ countries through ABB Group network. USD % of exports and hedging policy not separately disclosed.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Cash flow hedge accounting for USD receivables using forward exchange contracts. Sun Pharma hedges a portion of expected USD revenue through forwards and options.
inr_exposure.evidence: US business ~31% of total FY2024-25 revenue (largest single geography). Specialty products (Ilumya, Cequa, Winlevi) ~13% of US revenue. Total international revenue ~67% of total.

pli_scheme.evidence: Sun Pharma is a beneficiary of India's PLI scheme for Bulk Drugs (Key Starting Materials and APIs). Selected for production-linked incentives on critical API categories under Scheme-II.

china_plus_one.evidence: Divi's Laboratories explicitly highlights supply-chain diversification by global innovator pharma companies away from China as a key structural demand driver. Multiple top-10 global MNC pharma companies are cited as placing new orders for critical generic APIs and CDMO projects with Divi's specifically due to China supply-chain de-risking. The company has invested in backward integration for key starting materials to offer China-free supply chains.

crude_exposure.evidence: Raw material costs ~39% of revenue in FY2024-25. Key raw materials include solvents, reagents, and specialty chemicals that are partly petroleum-linked. Divi's backward integration model reduces direct crude oil exposure versus peers.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Natural hedge approach: USD import costs (raw materials) partially offset USD export receipts. The company earned forex gains of Rs 48 crore in FY25. Selective forward contract coverage for residual net exposure.
inr_exposure.evidence: ~88% of revenue is export (~52% Europe, ~17% US, ~19% other). Substantially all export revenues are USD/EUR denominated.

pli_scheme.evidence: Divi's Laboratories is a beneficiary of India's PLI scheme for pharmaceutical APIs and Key Starting Materials. Selected under Scheme-I for domestic manufacturing of critical bulk drugs.

rural.evidence: Rural demand improving for Royal Enfield motorcycles (tier-2/3 city and rural India expansion cited by management), but specific rural revenue % not disclosed. Eicher's primary demand driver is aspirational middle-class buyers in semi-urban and urban markets.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Eicher Motors (Royal Enfield) has a net cash position of approximately Rs 3,290 crore as of FY25. VE Commercial Vehicles (VECV) JV has some debt. Eicher standalone is effectively net cash; minimal floating rate liability.

inr_exposure.evidence: International (export) revenue ~14% of total FY2024-25 revenue. Royal Enfield exports motorcycles to 60+ countries; key export markets include South East Asia, UK, Europe, and North America. USD/EUR revenue % of total not separately disclosed.

rural.evidence: Radico Khaitan's distribution covers tier-2/3 cities and rural markets through 720,000 retail outlets. Management cited rising disposable incomes in tier-2 and rural India as a growth driver for IMFL premiumisation, but specific rural revenue % not disclosed.

govt_capex.evidence: CSD (Canteen Stores Department) is a significant channel for Radico Khaitan supplying alcohol to defence canteens. CSD revenue % not separately disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Radico Khaitan reduced total debt by 46.8% to approximately Rs 2 billion in FY25. Floating vs fixed rate breakdown not disclosed. Significant debt reduction lowers interest rate sensitivity.

crude_exposure.evidence: Key raw materials are Extra Neutral Alcohol (ENA) sourced from molasses (sugarcane) and grains — not crude oil derivatives. Glass bottles (packaging) have some indirect energy/crude cost linkage but this is not material or separately disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export revenue ~7% of FY2024-25 total revenue; key export markets include North America, UAE, UK, and South East Asia for premium IMFL brands (Rampur Whisky, Royal Ranthambore). USD hedging policy not specifically disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Gabriel India received orders from DAF Trucks (Netherlands) for shock absorbers (export component business), indicating growing international customer interest. However, there is no explicit China+1 supply-chain diversification narrative in management commentary; the international business remains small at ~3% of revenue.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Gabriel India is effectively debt-free with a net cash-positive balance sheet as of FY25. Not materially rate-sensitive on liability side.

crude_exposure.evidence: Gabriel India's key raw materials include steel tubes, polymers, and rubber seals. Some indirect crude oil linkage through polymers and rubber, but specific raw material cost % as a function of crude pricing is not disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export revenue ~3% of total FY2024-25 revenue; exports include shock absorbers and suspension components to OEM customers including DAF Trucks Netherlands.

rural.evidence: KSB India serves irrigation and agricultural water management sectors; PM-KUSUM solar pump scheme is an emerging opportunity. Specific rural revenue % not disclosed. KSB India uses January–December fiscal year; CY2024 = year ended December 2024.

govt_capex.evidence: KSB India serves government-linked sectors: Jal Jeevan Mission (village water supply pumps), nuclear power plants (NPCIL — KSB holds Type Approval for main coolant pumps), solar energy balance-of-plant, water utilities, and defence. Revenue % from government capex programs not explicitly disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export revenue ~17% of CY2024 total revenue; KSB India exports industrial pumps and valves to global KSB Group markets (Europe, Middle East, South East Asia).

china_plus_one.evidence: Bosch India MD Stefan Grosch explicitly stated in FY25 earnings commentary that 'China's loss is not necessarily India's gain' in the context of supply chain shifts, indicating Bosch India does not expect significant China+1 tailwinds for its manufacturing.

rural.evidence: Bosch India's Two-Wheeler and tractor segments serve rural and semi-urban markets. Management noted tractor segment growth (farm equipment, BSREM tractor systems). Rural segment revenue % not separately disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Bosch India has a net cash position of approximately Rs 1,016 crore as of FY25. Minimal floating rate liability.

crude_exposure.evidence: Bosch India's cost of materials consumed and purchases of traded goods is approximately 62% of revenue. Key materials include steel, aluminum die castings, electronics, and specialty chemicals. Some materials (polymers, rubber) have indirect crude linkage, but primary raw material exposure is to steel and aluminum prices.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export revenue ~10% of FY2024-25 total revenue. Bosch India exports auto components, industrial tools, and semiconductor test equipment primarily through Bosch Global Supply Chain. USD % of exports not separately disclosed.

pli_scheme.evidence: Bosch India is participating in the PLI scheme for automobile and auto components as a Component Champion under the Automotive PLI scheme for advanced automotive electronics and EV components.

china_plus_one.evidence: Rising preference for Indian fluorochemical suppliers amid China+1 sentiment is benefiting NFIL's export-led business. The company has started receiving new enquiries from companies looking for supply chain diversification out of China. NFIL developed backward integration through a 25% JV with the only fluorspar beneficiation company in India, reducing dependence on Chinese fluorspar supply.

rural.evidence: No mention of rural markets. NFIL is a B2B specialty fluorochemical manufacturer serving pharma, agrochemical, refrigeration, and industrial customers.

govt_capex.evidence: No government or infrastructure capex exposure disclosed. Customer base is global and domestic private-sector companies in pharma, agrochemicals, refrigerant OEMs, and specialty chemical industries.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Long-term debt primarily for capex on Dahej CMOS chemicals facility and new HF backward-integration plant. Floating vs fixed rate breakdown not disclosed in publicly accessible sources. Finance costs increased 4.5% YoY in FY25.

crude_exposure.evidence: Raw material costs ~Rs 1,039 crore for FY25 against total revenue ~Rs 2,349 crore (~44%). Key raw materials: hydrofluoric acid (HF), fluorspar (CaF2), and chloroform. No direct crude oil linkage; primary exposure is to fluorspar prices. Company is building a 40,000 TPA HF plant at Dahej for backward integration.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports ~65% of FY25 revenues; Q4FY25 exports were 77%. US accounts for approximately 20% of total sales. Significant USD revenue from long-term supply contracts with global pharma and specialty chemical companies. Specific hedging policy not disclosed in accessible sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: No credible source confirms NFIL as a PLI scheme beneficiary. Ministry of Chemicals announced PLI for specialty chemicals, but NFIL has not been publicly identified as a selected beneficiary in any available analyst report, company filing, or news source.

rural.evidence: B-30 (beyond top 30 cities) Average AUM approximately 18.2% of total Mutual Fund AUM as of FY2024-25. Nippon India MF has dedicated SIP campaigns and branch expansion targeting B-30 and T-30 cities to grow retail investor penetration. B-30 MAAUM grew faster than T-30 in FY25.

rate_sensitive.evidence: NAM-India has zero interest-bearing borrowings. Not rate-sensitive on liability side. Rate cuts benefit NAM-India's revenue (AUM side): lower rates drive inflows into fixed income/debt funds, improving total AUM and management fee income.

inr_exposure.evidence: NAM-India manages overseas/GIFT City fund of funds. USD-denominated revenue as % of total is negligible; all primary revenue is domestic rupee management fees.

china_plus_one.evidence: Garware Hi-Tech Films management acknowledges China as the main competitor in specialty polyester films globally. The company competes with Chinese manufacturers on price but has not explicitly positioned itself as a China+1 alternative; it differentiates on product quality and custom specifications for specialty applications.

rural.evidence: Garware Hi-Tech Films is a B2B specialty polyester films manufacturer. 100% of sales are to industrial/commercial customers (automotive aftermarket, solar lamination, agricultural greenhouse films). Zero rural retail exposure.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Garware Hi-Tech Films is effectively debt-free with a net cash-positive balance sheet as of FY25.

crude_exposure.evidence: Key raw materials are PTA (purified terephthalic acid) and MEG (mono ethylene glycol), both direct crude oil/naphtha derivatives. Raw material costs ~46.5% of revenue in FY2024-25. Direct crude-linked input cost volatility.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Net forward contract hedging: hedges net foreign exchange exposure (export receipts minus import payments) through forward exchange contracts in USD and EUR. Policy is to hedge net exposure rather than gross export revenue.
inr_exposure.evidence: US market ~48.5% of total revenue (largest geography). Total exports ~76.8% of revenue. Europe ~12.3%, Asia ex-China ~10.4%, others ~5.6%.

rural.evidence: B-30 (beyond top 30 cities) Monthly AAUM was Rs. 645 billion as of March 2025, representing ~17% of Mutual Fund AUM (total MF QAAUM Rs. 3,817 billion for Q4 FY25). B-30 MAAUM grew 12% YoY. Over 80% of ABSLAMC's 300+ branch locations are in B-30 cities, with 95+ dedicated emerging market locations.

govt_capex.evidence: ABSLAMC manages the Aditya Birla Sun Life Government Securities Fund (gilt fund). Fixed income (debt) AUM ~37% of total MF AUM. Specific share of government securities within fixed income AUM not separately disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: ABSLAMC has zero borrowings confirmed across multiple periods. Rate-sensitive on revenue side: rate cuts boost debt fund returns and AUM, driving management fee income. RBI cut repo rate 50bps in FY25. Fixed income QAAUM ~Rs. 1,500 billion (~37% of MF AUM). Debt fund AUM earns 24-25bps management fee vs equity at 68-69bps.

inr_exposure.evidence: Offshore AUM of ~INR 121 billion (~3% of total AUM of Rs. 4,056 billion) includes Cayman Islands funds investing in Indian-issued dollar bonds and GIFT City AIFs. USD-denominated revenue not separately quantified as % of total.

govt_capex.evidence: Schaeffler India serves railways (bearings for coaches, wagons, locomotive axle boxes), wind energy (main shaft and gearbox bearings), and renewable energy sectors. Government capex-linked revenue % not separately disclosed. Schaeffler India uses January–December fiscal year; CY2024 = year ended December 2024.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Schaeffler India has a net cash-positive balance sheet. Not materially rate-sensitive on liability side.

crude_exposure.evidence: Key raw materials include bearing-grade steel rings, engineering plastics (cages), and lubricants. Some indirect crude linkage through engineering plastics and lubricants; primary raw material exposure is to steel prices. Specific raw material cost % not disclosed in accessible sources.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export revenue ~17% of CY2024 total revenue; exports through Schaeffler Group global supply chain. Specific USD revenue % and hedging policy not disclosed.

pli_scheme.evidence: Schaeffler India is participating in the PLI scheme for automobile and auto components as a Component Champion, investing in EV-relevant components (e-Axle systems, actuators) that qualify for the Automotive PLI scheme.

rural.evidence: Pidilite's 'Emerging India' segment (tier-2/3 and rural markets) grew faster than Urban segment in FY2024-25. Specific Emerging India revenue % not separately disclosed in publicly accessible sources.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Pidilite Industries is effectively debt-free with no significant long-term borrowings. Not materially rate-sensitive on liability side.

crude_exposure.evidence: Vinyl Acetate Monomer (VAM) is Pidilite's key raw material (used in Fevicol and other adhesives) and is a direct crude oil/naphtha derivative. Raw material costs ~47% of revenue. VAM prices fluctuate with crude oil and are a key margin determinant.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Multi-source procurement and selective hedging for VAM price volatility; natural partial hedge as VAM is imported in USD while products are sold in INR domestically.
inr_exposure.evidence: Export revenue ~7% of FY2024-25 total revenue; exports include adhesives, construction chemicals, and art materials to South Asia, Middle East, and Africa.

rural.evidence: Avenue Supermarts (DMart) operates 415 stores as of March 2025, with cluster-based expansion increasingly targeting tier-2 and tier-3 cities. Specific revenue % from non-metro stores not disclosed. Store expansion strategy gradually penetrates smaller cities but revenue is not classified by rural vs urban in public disclosures.

rate_sensitive.evidence: DMart has near-zero net debt (owns most of its store properties). Not materially rate-sensitive on liability side.

inr_exposure.evidence: DMart is a 100% domestic Indian retailer with zero export revenue. No USD or foreign currency revenue.

crude_exposure.evidence: Crude oil derivatives (titanium dioxide, solvents, acrylic resins, vinyl acetate) constitute approximately 25-30% of Berger Paints' total raw material basket; total raw material costs ~55-60% of revenue. Crude price movements are a significant margin determinant.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export revenue ~8% of FY2024-25 total revenue; exports include decorative and industrial paints to South Asia, Middle East, and Africa. USD revenue % not separately disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Indian Hotels Co. (Taj Hotels) had nil net debt as of March 2025 (gross cash Rs 3,073 crore vs gross debt). Interest coverage ratio 13.4x in FY25. Not materially rate-sensitive on liability side.

inr_exposure.evidence: International (overseas hotel) operations contribute approximately 40% of consolidated revenue in FY2024-25, covering USA, UK, Middle East, Africa, and Maldives hotel properties and management contracts. Revenue in USD, GBP, AED, and other currencies. Specific USD revenue % not separately disclosed. export_pct represents consolidated international hotel revenue.
